title: WolfDesk Ticket Flows
subtitle: Every action, event and reaction in the WolfDesk help desk, from the Learning Domain-Driven Design example, built on Act.

slices.label: AgentSlice
slices.description: The desk: adds an agent, in one support category.

slices.label: TicketCreationSlice
slices.description: Opens, resolves and closes tickets, and assigns an agent when a ticket opens.

slices.label: TicketMessagingSlice
slices.description: Adds, delivers and acknowledges messages, and delivers each new message through the notification service.

slices.label: TicketOpsSlice
slices.description: Assigns, escalates and reassigns tickets, and escalates when a customer asks for it.

slices.label: TicketTimersSlice
slices.description: Declares no partial state of its own: four deferred reactions that call actions owned by other slices.

slices.label: TicketWebhooksSlice
slices.description: Declares no partial state of its own: one reaction that posts each escalation to an incident endpoint.

nodes.label: Customer
nodes.description: Opens tickets, writes messages, reads replies, asks for escalation. Owns the ticket (the mustBeUser precondition).

nodes.label: Support agent
nodes.description: The assigned agent. Answers and reads messages, resolves the ticket.

nodes.label: tickets
nodes.note: Drizzle table, one row per ticket
nodes.description: Projection folded from the full Ticket state and flushed in batches as upserts keyed on the stream.

nodes.label: assign
nodes.description: Asks the agents table for the agent with the fewest open tickets in the ticket's category, then invokes AssignTicket. With nobody free it throws a DeferSignal and looks again in a minute. Stops if the ticket was closed, resolved or assigned by hand meanwhile. Runs on its own target assign:<ticket>.

nodes.label: autoClose
nodes.description: Throws a DeferSignal until the ticket's closeAfter, then closes the ticket if nobody closed it first. Runs on its own target close:<ticket>.

nodes.label: autoEscalate
nodes.description: `.defer`red to escalateAfter on TicketAssigned. Escalates if the ticket is still open and not escalated. Target escalate:<ticket>.

nodes.label: deliver
nodes.description: Sends the message through the notification service, then marks it delivered. Up to 5 retries with exponential backoff and jitter.

nodes.label: escalate
nodes.description: Turns an escalation request into EscalateTicket.

nodes.label: autoReassign
nodes.description: Defers to reassignAfter, then reassigns the ticket unless an agent has read one of the customer's messages or the ticket is closed. Target reassign:<ticket>.

nodes.label: escalation webhook
nodes.description: webhook() from @rotorsoft/act-http on its own webhooks lane: 30 s lease, 2 s timeout, 3 retries with exponential backoff, Idempotency-Key, optional HMAC signing. All tickets share one target, ticket-escalation-webhooks.

nodes.label: autoReassignAgain
nodes.description: Each TicketReassigned pushes reassignAfter forward and re-arms the same check. The chain stops once an agent reads a customer message.

nodes.label: Notification service
nodes.description: deliverMessage(): the outbound channel. In development it fails the first WOLFDESK_DELIVERY_FAILS attempts per message so the backoff shows.

nodes.label: Incident endpoint
nodes.description: WOLFDESK_ESCALATION_WEBHOOK. The demo receiver verifies the signature and dedupes on the Idempotency-Key, so retries are safe.

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.description: An agent on the desk, one stream per agent, in one support category, with at most 5 open tickets, held by its schema whichever action takes a ticket. Declared by its own slice and by the creation and operations slices, whose actions load it: it's one state, drawn in each. A ticket with no agent loads none: its load is skipped, and TicketDropped with it.
nodes.schema:
name: string
supportCategoryId: string
open: number ≥ 0, ≤ 5

nodes.label: TicketTaken
nodes.description: Owned by Agent. An assign or a reassign may emit it because its .loads lists it.

nodes.label: TicketDropped
nodes.description: Owned by Agent. A reassign, or an assign to a new agent, frees the old agent's slot.

nodes.label: TicketDropped
nodes.description: Owned by Agent. A resolve or a close frees the slot, when the ticket still holds one. A ticket frees its slot once.

nodes.label: Desk manager
nodes.description: Adds agents to the desk.

nodes.label: AddAgent
preconditions: Agent must not be on the desk
nodes.schema:

supportCategoryId: uuid

nodes.label: AgentAdded
nodes.description: An agent joined the desk, in one support category.
nodes.schema:

nodes.label: agents
nodes.note: Drizzle table, one row per agent, with open tickets
nodes.description: Projection folded from Agent. The assign and reassign reactions read it to pick an agent. It can lag a stream, so it only suggests: the commit decides.

scenarios.title: Open to resolved
scenarios.summary: A customer opens a ticket, the system assigns an agent, they trade messages both ways and the agent resolves it.

steps.say: **Carla**, a customer, opens a ticket: Printer on fire, priority High.
The Ticket state is empty, so OpenTicket passes. **TicketOpened** commits at version 0 and carries her first message.
After the commit, the **assign** reaction picks the event up from the stream.

It picks an agent and invokes **AssignTicket** as the automation actor, with the event as `reactingTo`. It loads Ada's count, 2 of 5. This ticket has no agent yet, so its other load is a read of a placeholder.
One commit: **TicketAssigned** sets the agent and the deadlines, and **TicketTaken** counts it on Ada's stream, 3 of 5.
**Ada**, the agent, writes to Carla.
Two preconditions pass: the ticket is open and Ada is the assigned agent. **MessageAdded** commits.
The **deliver** reaction claims the stream.
It hands the message to the **notification service**.
Delivery worked, so it invokes **MarkMessageDelivered**.
**MessageDelivered** commits.
**Carla** reads Ada's reply. Only the receiver may acknowledge a message.
**MessageRead** commits.
**Carla** answers: it worked.
**MessageAdded** commits, addressed to Ada.
**deliver** reacts again, for the new message.
The notification service sends it to Ada.
It invokes **MarkMessageDelivered**.
**MessageDelivered** commits.
**Ada** reads Carla's message.
**MessageRead** commits. An agent has now read a customer message, which is the condition that stops any reassignment.
**Ada** marks the ticket resolved.
One commit: **TicketResolved** and **TicketDropped**, which frees Ada's slot. A later close frees nothing, so the slot is freed once. The tickets projection row shows the ticket resolved.

scenarios.title: Escalation chain
scenarios.summary: The ticket is assigned and past its escalation deadline. The customer asks for escalation, the system pages the outside world and keeps reassigning until an agent reads her message.

steps.say: **Carla** asks for escalation. Only the owner may, the ticket must be open and `escalateAfter` must have passed.
All checks pass. **TicketEscalationRequested** commits.
The **escalate** reaction picks it up.
It invokes **EscalateTicket** with the request data.
Not escalated before, so **TicketEscalated** commits. Two reactions listen to it.
The **escalation webhook** runs on its own `webhooks` lane, so a slow receiver never holds up the other reactions.
POST `{ ticket, escalationId }` to the **incident endpoint**, signed, with an Idempotency-Key.
**autoReassign** checks the ticket: nobody has read Carla's message, but `reassignAfter` is still ahead.
It throws a DeferSignal, sleeps until `reassignAfter`, wakes and invokes **ReassignTicket**.

One commit moves it: **TicketReassigned** sets the new agent and a later `reassignAfter`, **TicketDropped** frees Ada's slot and **TicketTaken** counts it on Grace's. A reassign that would overfill Grace refuses, and Ada keeps it.
**autoReassignAgain** arms the same check for the new deadline.
Grace does not answer either. At the deadline it reassigns again.
One commit again: **TicketReassigned** with Hugo, Grace drops it and Hugo takes it.
The chain re-arms once more.
**Hugo** reads Carla's message.
**MessageRead** commits on her message.
At the deadline the timer wakes, finds a customer message read by an agent and does nothing. The chain ends.

scenarios.title: Timers only
scenarios.summary: Nobody touches the ticket after it opens. Deferred reactions escalate it and later close it, with no polling jobs.

steps.say: **Carla** opens a ticket with a `closeAfter` deadline, then goes quiet.
**TicketOpened** commits with `closeAfter`.
**assign** reacts right away.
It invokes **AssignTicket**.
**TicketAssigned** commits with `escalateAfter` a day out.
**autoEscalate** is `.defer`red to `escalateAfter` on its own target `escalate:ticket-4823`, so a pending timer never holds the ticket's other reactions.
A day passes with no escalation. It wakes and invokes **EscalateTicket**.
**TicketEscalated** commits.
The escalation webhook fires.
The **incident endpoint** gets paged.
**autoReassign** arms its timer for `reassignAfter`.
Meanwhile **autoClose** has been waiting on `closeAfter` since the ticket opened.
Seven days later it wakes, finds the ticket still open and invokes **CloseTicket**.
**TicketClosed** commits, and **TicketDropped** frees Ada's slot in the same commit.
When the reassignment timer wakes, it sees `closedById` and does nothing.

scenarios.title: Retries and blocking
scenarios.summary: The outside world fails. Delivery recovers after two retries. The escalation webhook runs out of retries and blocks its target.

steps.say: **Carla** adds a message.
**MessageAdded** commits.
**deliver** claims the stream.
The channel fails twice. Each failure schedules the next attempt with exponential backoff and jitter, persisted on the stream so any worker honors it. The third attempt lands.
Now it invokes **MarkMessageDelivered**.
**MessageDelivered** commits.
**Carla** asks for escalation.
**TicketEscalationRequested** commits.
**escalate** reacts.
It invokes **EscalateTicket**.
**TicketEscalated** commits.
The **escalation webhook** claims its target.

The incident endpoint is down. After 4 attempts (`maxRetries` 3 + 1) the target `ticket-escalation-webhooks` blocks. All tickets share it, so later escalation webhooks wait until an operator calls `app.unblock`, which resumes from the watermark.

scenarios.title: Refused actions
scenarios.summary: The state refuses actions that break its rules. Nothing is committed, and the caller gets the error.

steps.say: **Carla** retries the OpenTicket action on the same stream.
The state already has a product, so the precondition **Cannot open twice** refuses it.
**Carla** asks for escalation too early.
`escalateAfter` is still ahead, so the state refuses.
**Ada** tries to mark her own message as read.
Only the receiver may acknowledge. The precondition reads the message id from the payload and refuses: an PreconditionError comes back.
Later, the inactivity timer closes the ticket.
**TicketClosed** commits, and **TicketDropped** frees Ada's slot.
**Carla** writes one more message.
The **Ticket must be open** precondition fails. A closed ticket accepts no more actions.

scenarios.title: A full agent
scenarios.summary: The agents table still shows Ada with 4, but her stream already holds 5. The assign reaction picks her, and Agent's schema refuses the commit. The retry finds the table caught up and picks Ben. Later the ticket moves again, and the count moves with it, in one commit.

steps.say: **Carla** opens a ticket.
**TicketOpened** commits.
The **assign** reaction picks up the event.
It asks the **agents** table for the fewest open tickets in this category. The table lags her stream: Ada shows **4**, tied with Ben and Cleo.
It picks **Ada**, and AssignTicket loads her count: really **5 of 5**.

steps.reject: Too big: expected number to be <=5
steps.say: Folding **TicketTaken** would make 6, so **Agent's schema refuses**, and nothing lands on either stream (`ValidationError`).
Now the **agents** table shows Ada at 5.
The reaction fails, and its retry asks again. The table has caught up: **Ben**, with 4 of 5. If every retry found a full agent, the stream would block until `app.unblock`.
One commit: **TicketAssigned** and **TicketTaken**. Ben holds 5 of 5.
A support agent hands the ticket to **Cleo**. Now both loads have events to emit: Ben's and Cleo's counts.
One commit across three streams: **TicketAssigned**, **TicketDropped** on Ben, **TicketTaken** on Cleo. A slot can't be lost between them.

scenarios.title: A new agent
scenarios.summary: A manager adds Dee to the desk. The next ticket in her category goes to her, since she holds the fewest.

steps.say: A manager adds **Dee** to the Billing desk.
**AgentAdded** lands on her own stream.
The **agents** table gets her row, with 0 open.
**Carla** opens a Billing ticket.
**TicketOpened** commits.
The **assign** reaction picks up the event.
It asks the table for the fewest open tickets in Billing: **Dee**, with 0. Ada has 3.
AssignTicket loads Dee's stream, and the stream has the real count.
One commit: **TicketAssigned** and **TicketTaken**. Dee holds 1 of 5.
The table catches up: Dee, 1 open.

scenarios.title: Waiting for an agent
scenarios.summary: Everyone in the category is full, so a new ticket waits. When Ben resolves a ticket, his slot frees, and the next look assigns the waiting ticket to him.

steps.say: **Carla** opens a ticket.
**TicketOpened** commits.
The **assign** reaction picks up the event.
The table shows nobody free: Ada and Ben hold **5 of 5**. The reaction throws a `DeferSignal` and **the ticket waits**, unassigned. Nothing fails, and nothing blocks.
Meanwhile **Ben** resolves another ticket.
One commit: **TicketResolved** and **TicketDropped**. Ben holds 4 of 5.
The **agents** table shows Ben's free slot.
A minute after it deferred, the reaction wakes and asks again: **Ben**, with 4 of 5.
AssignTicket loads Ben's stream.
One commit: **TicketAssigned** and **TicketTaken**. The waiting ticket has its agent, and Ben holds 5 of 5.
